claims.text: The untreated high-entropy-alloy intermediate layer lacks specialized grain-boundary and nanoprecipitate engineering.
Controlled annealing will refine the grain structure of the high-entropy alloy.
Controlled annealing will induce in-situ formation of nanoscale ceramic precipitates.
The annealing treatment will produce uniformly dispersed nanoscale ceramic precipitates in the alloy matrix.
Refined grain boundaries reduce phonon scattering.
The ceramic precipitates will form aligned channels for heat transport.
The aligned precipitate channels will facilitate heat transfer.
The combined grain-boundary and precipitate changes will enhance thermal conductivity without compromising mechanical strength or structural integrity.
The treatment may improve the mechanical strength of the alloy.
The treated alloy will show more than a 10% increase in thermal conductivity relative to the untreated baseline.
The treated alloy will maintain or enhance resistance to mechanical deformation relative to the untreated baseline.
The predicted thermal and mechanical benefits will hold at temperatures from approximately 600 to 800 degrees Celsius.
The predicted benefits will hold under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading representative of plasma-facing components.
